objective: Proof: with counts never below the next round demand the pattern is the rank-truncated order of ideals of its one-parent junctions (Birkhoff); one count for every join survives exactly when it equals the first knot size (stall rounds otherwise), giving the a-fold product of counting chains with bond balls of order r^a; with the cap of three exactly three; the fewest counts close one knot into the 2^a pattern; the distance reader generalised.
status: Proved 2026-11-18 (referee pending): with no stall the pattern grown by the cubic study's joining rule under any count rule is the down-closed sets of the descent order of its offshoots (Birkhoff), so a count rule only places offshoots (T1); one count for every join survives exactly at the first knot's size a, building the a-fold counting pattern, otherwise stalls at round 2, 4 or 3 (T2); with groups of at most three only a = 3 (T3); the fewest counts close one knot into the 2^a pattern and conserve the chains of demand 1 from any hand-over, any number (T4); bond balls of the a-fold pattern are Theta(r^a) (T5); the threshold reader recovers every junction under one count (T6); cheapest one-count growth is at a = 3 (Corollary 2.1).
title: What the joining policy builds when the count is free
